st: Stir the breadcrumbs and milk together in a large bowl and let stand for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the beef, pork, onion, egg, [[1 tsp]] salt, the pepper and allspice. Mix gently with your hands until just combined.
Wet your hands and roll the mixture into small balls about the size of a walnut. Put them on a tray.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Brown the meatballs in batches for 8 minutes each, turning, until cooked through to 160°F/71°C.
Move the meatballs to a plate and cover to keep warm.
Melt the remaining [[2 tbsp]] butter in the same pan. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Slowly pour in the broth, whisking, and simmer for 5 minutes until thickened.
Stir in the cream, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the soy sauce. Simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Return the meatballs to the gravy and warm for 3 minutes. Serve with potatoes and lingonberry jam.

ing: very fresh, skin on, center cut
st: Run your fingers over the salmon and pull out any pin bones with tweezers. Use salmon that is very fresh and meant to be eaten raw or cured.
Mix the salt, sugar and crushed pepper in a small bowl.
Lay a large sheet of plastic wrap on the counter. Spread half the dill in a bed the size of the fillet.
Place the salmon skin side down on the dill. Rub the salt mixture all over the flesh and cover with the rest of the dill.
Wrap the fish tightly in the plastic, then put it in a dish and set a plate on top with a couple of cans as weights.
Refrigerate for 48 hours, flipping the package every 12 hours and spooning juices back over it.
Unwrap, scrape off the dill and extra cure, and pat dry. Do not rinse unless it is too salty.
Slice very thin on a diagonal, leaving the skin behind. Serve with the mustard sauce, bread and extra dill.

ing: peeled and cut into thin matchsticks
2 oz cans, drained, brine saved (Swedish ansjovis)
st: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and grease a medium baking dish with [[1 tbsp]] butter.
Melt [[1 tbsp]] butter in a skillet and cook the onions for 8 minutes over low heat until soft but not browned.
Layer half the potatoes in the baking dish. Spread over the onions and the sprats, then top with the remaining potatoes.
Sprinkle with the pepper. The fish is salty, so add salt only if needed.
Pour [[0.5 cup]] of the cream and a splash of the fish brine over the top, and sprinkle with the breadcrumbs.
Dot with the remaining [[1 tbsp]] butter, and bake for 20 minutes.
Pour in the remaining [[1 cup]] cream and bake for 30 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender and the top is golden and bubbling.
Let it rest for 10 minutes before serving hot.
Whisk the milk, eggs, flour and salt in a large bowl until you have a smooth batter.
Cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat for 8 minutes until crisp. Drain on paper towels and keep warm. Wipe out the pan.
Grate the potatoes on the coarse side of a box grater straight into the batter and stir. Do not squeeze out the liquid.
Melt a little of the butter in the skillet over medium heat.
Spoon in about [[0.25 cup]] batter per pancake and press thin with the back of the spoon. Fry in batches without crowding.
Cook for 4 minutes per side until deep golden brown and crisp at the edges, as the potato must cook through.
Add more butter to the pan between batches. Keep the finished pancakes warm in a low oven.
Serve hot with the bacon and lingonberry jam.

ing: peeled and cut into small cubes
st: Boil the potato cubes in salted water for 5 minutes until just barely tender. Drain and let them dry well.
Heat the oil and [[1 tbsp]] butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the potatoes in a single layer, stirring only now and then, for 12 minutes until crisp and golden.
Move them to a plate. Cook the sausage and beef in the same pan for 6 minutes until browned.
Add [[1 tbsp]] butter and the onion and cook for 4 minutes until soft.
Return the potatoes to the pan, season with the salt and pepper, and toss for 3 minutes until everything is hot and crisp.
In a separate pan, melt the remaining [[1 tbsp]] butter and fry the eggs sunny side up.
Serve the hash topped with a fried egg and the pickled beets on the side.
Soak the peas in plenty of cold water overnight, or for at least 8 hours. Drain and rinse them.
Put the peas, pork, onion and [[8 cups]] fresh water in a large pot. Bring to a boil and skim off any foam and loose skins.
Add the thyme and marjoram. Reduce the heat, partly cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours, stirring now and then, until the peas are very soft.
Lift out the pork. Remove the skin and bones, and cut the meat into small pieces.
Return the meat to the pot and mash some of the peas against the pot for a thicker texture, if you like.
Simmer 15 minutes more. Add the salt and taste, adjusting if needed.
Serve in warm bowls with mustard stirred in at the table.

ing: 1 tsp zest and juice of half
st: Pat the shrimp very dry with paper towels, then chop them into small pieces.
In a bowl, stir the mayonnaise, sour cream, chopped dill, lemon zest, a squeeze of lemon juice, the onion, salt and pepper.
Fold in the shrimp gently. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then chill for 10 minutes.
Cut each bread slice in half diagonally, or leave them whole, as you prefer.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Fry the bread for 2 minutes per side until crisp and golden. Drain on paper towels.
Pile the shrimp mixture on the warm toast.
Top with the roe and a sprig of dill, and serve right away.

ing: softened, for the dough (1/4 cup) and filling (1/4 cup)
st: Stir the warm milk, yeast and a spoonful of the sugar in a large bowl. Let stand 5 minutes until foamy.
Add the remaining sugar, flour, cardamom, salt, one egg and [[0.25 cup]] soft butter. Mix and knead for 8 minutes until smooth and slightly sticky.
Cover the dough and let it rise until doubled in size.
Mix [[0.25 cup]] soft butter with the brown sugar and cinnamon into a thick paste.
Roll the dough into a large rectangle. Spread the filling evenly all over it.
Roll up tightly from the long side. Cut the roll into 12 slices with a sharp knife or floss.
Place the buns cut side up on lined baking sheets, cover and let rise for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with pearl sugar. Bake for 10 minutes until golden.
Cool for 10 minutes on a rack before serving warm.

ing: green, or white colored with green food coloring
st: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line the bottom of a 9 inch springform pan with parchment. Beat the eggs and [[0.75 cup]] sugar for 8 minutes until pale, thick and tripled in volume.
Sift the flour, cornstarch and baking powder over the eggs and fold in gently. Pour into the pan and bake for 30 minutes. Cool completely, then slice into three even layers.

For the custard, whisk the milk, yolks, [[0.33 cup]] sugar, [[3 tbsp]] cornstarch and [[1 tsp]] vanilla in a saucepan. Cook over medium heat, whisking, until it thickens and bubbles. Boil for 1 minute.
Cover the surface with plastic wrap and cool completely in the refrigerator.
Whip the cream with the remaining [[1 tsp]] vanilla until stiff peaks form.
Put the bottom sponge layer on a plate and spread with half the jam, then half the custard. Add a layer of whipped cream.
Add the second sponge layer and repeat with jam and custard. Top with the third layer, and pile the rest of the cream on top into a high dome.
Dust a counter with powdered sugar. Roll the marzipan into a large thin circle and drape it over the cake, smoothing down the sides. Trim the excess.
Chill for at least 2 hours to set, then dust with powdered sugar and slice.

ing: warm, plus 3 tbsp for the filling
st: Stir [[1 cup]] warm milk with the yeast and a spoonful of the sugar. Let stand 5 minutes until foamy.
Add the rest of the sugar, flour, cardamom, salt, one egg and the butter. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and soft.
Cover and let the dough rise until doubled.
Divide into 12 balls and shape each smooth and round. Place them on lined baking sheets, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Brush the buns with beaten egg and bake for 15 minutes until golden. Cool completely on a rack.
Cut a lid off the top of each bun and scoop out some of the inside into a bowl.
Mix the scooped crumbs with the grated almond paste and [[3 tbsp]] milk into a thick paste.
Whip the cream to stiff peaks. Spoon the almond paste into each bun, pipe or spoon in whipped cream, and set the lid on top.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve the same day.
Mix the rye flour, all-purpose flour, yeast, caraway seeds and salt in a large bowl.
Add the warm water, melted butter and honey. Stir to a firm dough, adding a spoonful more water if it is crumbly.
Knead for 5 minutes on a floured counter. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Divide the dough into 4 pieces.
Roll each piece out very thin, as thin as you can, on parchment dusted with rye flour.
Prick all over with a fork so the bread stays flat. Cut into rectangles or leave whole.
Bake for 15 minutes, then lower the oven to 300°F (150°C) and bake for 10 minutes more until dry and crisp.
Cool completely on a rack, where the bread crisps further. Store in an airtight container.
